report_title: P.I.T.C.H. Final Report Performance Scaffold (Production Kubernetes)
purpose: This dataset captures the final performance-evaluation campaign against the production Kubernetes deployment of P.I.T.C.H. using k6. It replaces ad hoc development-host measurements with a repeatable Kubernetes deployment while preserving the experiment families that are executable in the current application.
dataset_summary: The final production dataset targets the P.I.T.C.H. gateway running in a production Kubernetes cluster and exposed to k6 through https://api.pitchapp.ca. Results are organized by workload family so the final report can quantify steady-state latency, throughput, error rate, overload behavior, AI scenario-generation behavior, mixed workload behavior, and Kubernetes replica scaling.

environment.sut_deployment: Production Kubernetes deployment exposed at https://api.pitchapp.ca. For k6, use BASE_URL=https://api.pitchapp.ca because the workload scripts append /api/v1 paths internally.
observability: kubectl top pod/node when metrics-server is available

load_generator_topology.summary: The system under test runs inside a production Kubernetes cluster and k6 targets the public API endpoint. This gives a production Kubernetes evaluation while preserving the same workload matrix used for the final report.
load_generator_topology.ta_feedback: This production Kubernetes campaign improves deployment realism and repeatability. The final report should avoid overgeneralizing beyond the measured workload, endpoint, and campaign configuration.

threats_to_validity: Production Kubernetes resource allocation, managed backing services, and public-network variability can affect end-to-end latency.
Ingress, load-balancer routing, and public-network variability can affect measured latency.
The Helm values and replica settings should be recorded with each campaign before interpreting absolute throughput.
The PostgreSQL image did not include pgvector, so the public statistics workload used a minimal seeded schema for the Session, users, and teams tables required by the measured endpoint.
AI and mixed AI workloads were executed with the OpenAI key configured in apps/api/.env and an LLM routing entry that selects gpt-4o-mini for cost control.
If only the gateway deployment is scaled during the replica experiment, results should be interpreted as gateway-pod scaling rather than full microservice scaling.
The current application does not expose a verified cache-off toggle, so cache-comparison results are out of scope unless that runtime gate is implemented later.
limitation_handling: Keep this production Kubernetes dataset analytically separate from the older Docker Compose or development-host dataset and from any public Kubernetes dataset.
Record the exact hardware, cluster name, namespace, image tag, Helm values file, and replica settings used for each campaign.
Report production Kubernetes results as reproducibility and relative-scaling evidence, not as production SLA evidence.
Correlate latency cliffs and failure behavior with Kubernetes pod status, pod logs, restart counts, resource pressure, and backing-service observations before drawing bottleneck conclusions.
final_delivery_focus: Collect the full production Kubernetes experiment matrix with perf/scripts/run-production-k8s-campaign.sh.
Run python3 scripts/generate_perf_report.py --config perf/report_datasets/final-production-k8s.json after collecting results.
Use the generated tables and charts as the primary quantitative source for the final report's production Kubernetes evaluation section.
Frame conclusions around measured behavior across workloads and replica counts.

scenarios.label: baseline
notes: Collect low-load baseline runs against the production Kubernetes gateway before the scaling campaigns begin.
